task: Choose the correct option: My brother hates ___ early.
wrong options / checks: get up | gets up | to getting up
explanation shown to learner: *like, love, hate* + *-ing* (or *to* + verb): *I like cooking.* Not the base verb: not *I like cook*.
explanation in Latvian: *like, love, hate* + darbības vārds ar *-ing* (vai to + pamatforma): *I like cooking.* Nevis pamatforma: nevis *I like cook.*

task: My dad loves ___ old films. (watch)
explanation shown to learner: *like, love, hate* + *-ing* (or *to* + verb): *I like cooking.* Not the base verb: not *I like cook*.
explanation in Latvian: *like, love, hate* + darbības vārds ar *-ing* (vai to + pamatforma): *I like cooking.* Nevis pamatforma: nevis *I like cook.*

task: Put the words in order to make a question.
correct answer: do you want to come with us
explanation shown to learner: *want* + *to* + base verb: *I want to go.* Not *I want go* or *I want going*. In a question the helping verb (or *am / is / are*) goes before the subject.
explanation in Latvian: *want + to* + pamatforma: *I want to go.* Nevis *I want go* vai *I want going.* Jautājumā palīgdarbības vārds (vai *am / is / are*) stāv pirms teikuma priekšmeta.

task: I want ___ my own café one day. (open)
explanation shown to learner: *want* + *to* + base verb: *I want to go.* Not *I want go* or *I want going*.
explanation in Latvian: *want + to* + pamatforma: *I want to go.* Nevis *I want go* vai *I want going.*

task: My parents want ___ ___ a dog.
explanation shown to learner: *want* + *to* + base verb: *I want to go.* Not *I want go* or *I want going*.
explanation in Latvian: *want + to* + pamatforma: *I want to go.* Nevis *I want go* vai *I want going.*

task: Which sentence has a mistake?
correct answer: Ben likes play tennis on Sundays.
wrong options / checks: I want to visit Prague in May. | We love walking in the forest. | Do you like working from home?
explanation shown to learner: *like, love, hate* + *-ing* (or *to* + verb): *Ben likes playing tennis.* Not the base verb: not *likes play*.
explanation in Latvian: Tulkojot burtiski *Benam* patīk spēlēt → *Ben likes play.* Angļu valodā pēc *like, love, hate* lieto darbības vārdu ar *-ing* (vai to + pamatforma): *Ben likes playing tennis.*

task: Does your partner like ___ computer games? (play)
explanation shown to learner: *like, love, hate* + *-ing* (or *to* + verb): *I like cooking.* Not the base verb: not *I like cook*.
explanation in Latvian: *like, love, hate* + darbības vārds ar *-ing* (vai to + pamatforma): *I like cooking.* Nevis pamatforma: nevis *I like cook.*

task: Correct the mistake: Maria wants take a taxi to the airport.
correct answer: Maria wants to take a taxi to the airport.
explanation shown to learner: *want* + *to* + base verb: *Maria wants to take a taxi.* Not *wants take*.
explanation in Latvian: Tulkojot burtiski gribu iet → *I want go.* Angļu valodā pēc *want* vajag to + pamatforma: *Maria wants to take a taxi.*

task: Say it another way with *love*: Cooking is my favourite hobby.
correct answer: I love cooking. | I love to cook. | I really love cooking. | I really love to cook. | I love cooking very much.
explanation shown to learner: *like, love, hate* + *-ing* (or *to* + verb): *I like cooking.* Not the base verb: not *I like cook*.
explanation in Latvian: *like, love, hate* + darbības vārds ar *-ing* (vai to + pamatforma): *I like cooking.* Nevis pamatforma: nevis *I like cook.*

task: Put the words in order.
correct answer: my son doesn't want to learn to drive
explanation shown to learner: *want* + *to* + base verb, and *learn* + *to* + base verb: *My son doesn't want to learn to drive.* Not *want learn* or *want learning*.
explanation in Latvian: *want + to* + pamatforma, un arī *learn + to* + pamatforma: *My son doesn't want to learn to drive.* Nevis *want learn* vai *want learning*.

task: Choose the correct option: Tom wants ___ a bigger flat.
explanation shown to learner: *want* + *to* + base verb: *Tom wants to find a bigger flat.* Not *wants find*, *wants finding* or *wants to finding*.
explanation in Latvian: *want + to* + pamatforma: *Tom wants to find a bigger flat.* Nevis *wants find, wants finding* vai *wants to finding*.

task: My grandma loves ___ photos to the family.
explanation shown to learner: *love* + *-ing* (or *to* + verb): *My grandma loves sending photos.* Not the base verb or the *-s* form: not *loves send*, not *loves sends*.
explanation in Latvian: *love* + darbības vārds ar *-ing* (vai to + pamatforma): *My grandma loves sending photos.* Nevis *loves send* vai *loves sends*.

task: Choose the correct option: We visited three ___ on our trip.
explanation shown to learner: Consonant + *-y*: the *y* changes to *-ies*: *city → cities, country → countries, party → parties*.
explanation in Latvian: Līdzskanis + *-y*: *y* pārvēršas par *-ies*: *city → cities, country → countries, party → parties*.

task: Choose the correct option: I work late two ___ a week.
explanation shown to learner: Vowel + *-y* just adds *-s*: *day → days, key → keys, boy → boys*.
explanation in Latvian: Ja vārds beidzas ar *-ay, -ey, -oy*, pievieno vienīgi *-s*: *day → days, key → keys, boy → boys*.

task: Which sentence is correct?
correct answer: We bought two watches and three bags.
wrong options / checks: We bought two watchs and three bags. | We bought two watches and three bages. | We bought two watch and three bags.
explanation shown to learner: *watch* ends in *-ch*, so *watches*. *bag* just adds *-s*: *bags*.
explanation in Latvian: *watch* beidzas ar *-ch*, tāpēc *watches*. Vārdam *bag* pievieno vienīgi *-s*: *bags*.

task: Which sentence has a mistake?
correct answer: Our town has two new librarys.
wrong options / checks: We stayed in Rome for five days. | I always wash the dishes by hand. | Tom has two brothers and a sister.
explanation shown to learner: *library* ends in consonant + *-y*: *libraries*. (*days*: vowel + *-y*, only *-s*. *dishes*: *-sh* + *-es*.)
explanation in Latvian: *library* beidzas ar līdzskani + *-y*: *libraries*. (*days*: *-ay* beigās vienīgi *-s*. *dishes*: pēc *-sh* nāk *-es*.)

task: We need two big ___ for the books.
explanation shown to learner: After *-s, -sh, -ch, -x* the plural adds *-es*: *bus → buses, dish → dishes, watch → watches, box → boxes*.
explanation in Latvian: Pēc *-s, -sh, -ch, -x* daudzskaitlī pievieno *-es*: *bus → buses, dish → dishes, watch → watches, box → boxes*.

task: There are lots of ___ in December.
explanation shown to learner: Consonant + *-y*: the *y* changes to *-ies*: *city → cities, country → countries, party → parties*.
explanation in Latvian: Līdzskanis + *-y*: *y* pārvēršas par *-ies*: *city → cities, country → countries, party → parties*.

task: I've got three ___ for the office. (key)
explanation shown to learner: Vowel + *-y* just adds *-s*: *day → days, key → keys, boy → boys*.
explanation in Latvian: Ja vārds beidzas ar *-ay, -ey, -oy*, pievieno vienīgi *-s*: *day → days, key → keys, boy → boys*.

task: I have two English ___ a week. (class)
explanation shown to learner: After *-s, -sh, -ch, -x* the plural adds *-es*: *bus → buses, dish → dishes, watch → watches, box → boxes*.
explanation in Latvian: Pēc *-s, -sh, -ch, -x* daudzskaitlī pievieno *-es*: *bus → buses, dish → dishes, watch → watches, box → boxes*.

task: Start with *Two*: The bus is late.
correct answer: Two buses are late. | Two busses are late.
explanation shown to learner: More than one: *bus → buses* (after *-s* add *-es*), and the verb is plural too: *are*.
explanation in Latvian: Vairāk nekā viens: *bus → buses* (pēc *-s* nāk *-es*), un darbības vārds arī ir daudzskaitlī: *are*.

task: Choose the correct option: The shops here ___.
wrong options / checks: very expensive | are very expensives | very expensives
explanation shown to learner: After a noun the adjective needs *be*: *The shops are expensive.* The adjective never takes *-s*: not *expensives*.
explanation in Latvian: Aiz lietvārda īpašības vārdam vajag *be*: *The shops are expensive.* Īpašības vārdam nekad nepievieno *-s*: nevis *expensives*.

task: Put the words in order.
correct answer: she has a very good job
explanation shown to learner: An adjective goes before the noun: *a very good job* (not *a job very good*).
explanation in Latvian: Īpašības vārds stāv pirms lietvārda: *a very good job* (nevis *a job very good*).

task: Use the words in brackets: I need two ___ for the trip. (bag / big)
explanation shown to learner: Only the noun takes *-s*; the adjective stays the same and goes first: *two big bags* (not *two bigs bags*, *two bags big*).
explanation in Latvian: Tulkojot burtiski, divas lielas somas: latviešu valodā īpašības vārdam ir daudzskaitlis, angļu valodā nav. *-s* saņem tikai lietvārds, un īpašības vārds ir pirms tā: *two big bags* (nevis *two bigs bags, two bags big*).

task: We have two ___ ___ in our garden.
explanation shown to learner: Only the noun takes *-s*; the adjective stays the same and goes first: *two big bags* (not *two bigs bags*, *two bags big*).
explanation in Latvian: Tulkojot burtiski, divas lielas somas: latviešu valodā īpašības vārdam ir daudzskaitlis, angļu valodā nav. *-s* saņem tikai lietvārds, un īpašības vārds ir pirms tā: *two big bags* (nevis *two bigs bags, two bags big*).

task: Which sentence has a mistake?
correct answer: We rented a car small for the week.
wrong options / checks: The lesson was short and useful. | I need two new batteries for my camera. | Her flat has big windows.
explanation shown to learner: The adjective goes before the noun: *a small car*. After *be* it can stand alone (*The lesson was short*), and it has no *-s* (*new batteries*).
explanation in Latvian: Īpašības vārds stāv pirms lietvārda: *a small car*. Aiz *be* tas var stāvēt viens (*The lesson was short*), un tam nav *-s* (*new batteries*).

task: Use the words in brackets: My new headphones ___. (comfortable / very / be)
correct answer: are very comfortable | were very comfortable
explanation shown to learner: After a noun the adjective needs *be*: *The shops are expensive.* The adjective never takes *-s*: not *expensives*.
explanation in Latvian: Aiz lietvārda īpašības vārdam vajag *be*: *The shops are expensive.* Īpašības vārdam nekad nepievieno *-s*: nevis *expensives*.

task: Put the words in order.
correct answer: my grandmother is very active for her age
wrong options / checks: also accepted: for her age my grandmother is very active
explanation shown to learner: After *be* the adjective comes alone, without a noun: *My grandmother is very active.*
explanation in Latvian: Aiz *be* īpašības vārds var stāvēt viens, bez lietvārda: *My grandmother is very active.*

task: The rooms in this hotel ___ very ___.
explanation shown to learner: After a noun the adjective needs *be*: *The shops are expensive.* The adjective never takes *-s*: not *expensives*.
explanation in Latvian: Aiz lietvārda īpašības vārdam vajag *be*: *The shops are expensive.* Īpašības vārdam nekad nepievieno *-s*: nevis *expensives*.

task: Start with *Our*: We have very nice neighbours.
correct answer: Our neighbours are very nice. | Our neighbours are nice. | Our neighbours are really nice.
explanation shown to learner: The adjective moves after *be* and stays without *-s*: *Our neighbours are very nice.* (not *very nices*).
explanation in Latvian: Īpašības vārds pāriet aiz *be* un paliek bez *-s*: *Our neighbours are very nice.* (nevis *very nices*).

task: Choose the correct option: What time ___ you usually finish work?
explanation shown to learner: *usually* shows a habit, so the present simple: *What time do you usually finish work?* *Are you finishing* is about now or a plan; without *do* the question is not correct.
explanation in Latvian: *usually* norāda uz ieradumu, tāpēc Present Simple: *What time do you usually finish work?* *Are you finishing* ir par tagadni vai plānu; bez *do* jautājums ir kļūdains.

task: Which sentence has a mistake?
correct answer: Look! Our bus comes round the corner.
wrong options / checks: We usually have dinner at seven. | My brother is sleeping at the moment. | Does your shop open on Sundays?
explanation shown to learner: *Look!* shows it is happening now: *Look! Our bus is coming round the corner.* The other three are correct: a habit, an action now, a question about a regular time.
explanation in Latvian: *Look*! norāda, ka tas notiek tagad: *Look*! *Our bus is coming round the corner.* Pārējie trīs teikumi ir bez kļūdām: ieradums, darbība tagad, jautājums par regulāru laiku. Tulkojot burtiski, latviešu tagadne dod *Our bus comes*; angļu valodā tagad notiekošam vajag *is coming*.

task: Put the words in order.
correct answer: she usually swims but today she is running
wrong options / checks: also accepted: usually she swims but today she is running | she usually swims but she is running today | today she is running but she usually swims | she is running today but she usually swims | today she is running but usually she swims
explanation shown to learner: *usually* + present simple (*she usually swims*), *today* + present continuous (*today she is running*).
explanation in Latvian: *usually* + Present Simple (*she usually swims*), *today* + Present Continuous (*today she is running*).

task: Can I call you back? I ___ dinner.
explanation shown to learner: The person is eating dinner at this moment, so *I am having dinner*. *I have dinner* is a habit (*I have dinner at seven*).
explanation in Latvian: Cilvēks šobrīd ēd vakariņas, tāpēc *I am having dinner.* *I have dinner* ir ieradums (*I have dinner at seven*).

task: Look! Dad ___ the dishes. He never ___ that! (wash / do)
explanation shown to learner: *Look!*: happening now, *is washing*. *never*: a habit, present simple with *he*: *does*.
explanation in Latvian: *Look*!: notiek tagad, *is washing*. *never*: ieradums, Present Simple ar *he*: *does*.

task: Rewrite the sentence about this moment. Start with *Right now*: My sister reads the news on her phone.
correct answer: Right now my sister is reading the news on her phone. | Right now my sister's reading the news on her phone.
explanation shown to learner: *Right now*: an action in progress, *is reading*. *She reads the news* is a habit.
explanation in Latvian: *Right now*: darbība norisinās, *is reading*. *She reads the news* ir ieradums.

task: Which sentence has a mistake?
wrong options / checks: Were you at the gym on Monday? | My keys weren't in my bag. | We were in Riga last weekend.
explanation shown to learner: *I / he / she / it* + *was*; *you / we / they* + *were*. A plural noun (*the tickets*) = *they*: *The tickets were …*
explanation in Latvian: *I / he / she / it + was; you / we / they + were.* Daudzskaitļa lietvārds (*the tickets*) = *they*: *The tickets were* …

task: ___ your parents at the wedding?
explanation shown to learner: A question with *be* starts with *Was / Were*, without *did*: *Were your parents …?* *your parents* = *they*, so *Were*.
explanation in Latvian: Jautājums ar *be* sākas ar *Was / Were*, bez *did*: *Were your parents* …? *your parents = they*, tāpēc *Were*.

task: The shops ___ busy yesterday.
explanation shown to learner: Negative of *be*: *wasn't / weren't*, without *didn't*. *the shops* = *they*: *The shops weren't busy.*
explanation in Latvian: *be* noliegums: *wasn't / weren't*, bez *didn't*. *the shops = they*: *The shops weren't busy.*

task: Put the words in order.
explanation shown to learner: Question word + *were* + *you*: *Where were you …?* With *you* it is always *were*, and *be* needs no *did*.
explanation in Latvian: Jautājamais vārds + *were + you*: *Where were you* …? Ar *you* vienmēr ir *were*. Ar *be* nelieto *did*.

task: Put the words in order.
explanation shown to learner: Question word + *was / were* + subject: *Why was your phone off?* No *did* with *be*.
explanation in Latvian: Jautājamais vārds + *was / were* + teik. priekšmets: *Why was your phone off?* Ar *be* nelieto *did*.

task: Make a yes/no question: The exam was difficult.
correct answer: Was the exam difficult? | Was it difficult?
explanation shown to learner: Move *was* in front of the subject: *Was the exam difficult?* No *did*: not *Did the exam be difficult?*
explanation in Latvian: *was* pārceļ pirms teikuma priekšmeta: *Was the exam difficult?* Bez *did*: nevis *Did the exam be difficult?*

task: Which sentence has a mistake?
correct answer: I put a few salt in the soup.
wrong options / checks: I speak a little German. | There are a few museums in our town. | How much water do you drink every day?
explanation shown to learner: *salt* is uncountable, so *a little salt*, not *a few salt*. *a few* goes with plural nouns: *a few museums*.
explanation in Latvian: *salt* ir neskaitāms lietvārds, tāpēc *a little salt*, nevis *a few salt*. *a few* lieto ar daudzskaitļa lietvārdiem: *a few museums*.

task: Can you wait ___ minutes, please?
wrong options / checks: bank: a few | a little | much
explanation shown to learner: *a few* + plural noun = a small number: *a few minutes, a few times.* *a little* goes with uncountable nouns: *a little milk.*
explanation in Latvian: *a few* lieto ar daudzskaitļa lietvārdiem: *a few minutes, a few times*. *a little* lieto ar neskaitāmiem lietvārdiem: *a little milk*.

task: Write *a few* or *a little*: I go to the gym ___ times a week.
explanation shown to learner: *a few* + plural noun = a small number: *a few minutes, a few times.* *a little* goes with uncountable nouns: *a little milk.*
explanation in Latvian: *a few* lieto ar daudzskaitļa lietvārdiem: *a few minutes, a few times*. *a little* lieto ar neskaitāmiem lietvārdiem: *a little milk*.

task: Write *a few* or *a little*: Can I have ___ milk in my tea?
explanation shown to learner: *a little* + uncountable noun = a small amount: *a little milk, a little salt.* *a few* goes with plural nouns: *a few eggs.*
explanation in Latvian: *a little* lieto ar neskaitāmiem lietvārdiem: *a little milk, a little salt*. *a few* lieto ar daudzskaitļa lietvārdiem: *a few eggs*.

task: Say it another way with *a few* or *a little*: I speak some Spanish, but not much.
correct answer: I speak a little Spanish. | I can speak a little Spanish. | I know a little Spanish. | I speak a little Spanish, but not much. | I speak a few words of Spanish. | I know a few words of Spanish. | I can speak a few words of Spanish. | I speak a little bit of Spanish. | I can speak a little bit of Spanish. | I only speak a little Spanish. | I can only speak a little Spanish.
explanation shown to learner: *a few* + plural noun (*a few words, a few shops*), *a little* + uncountable noun (*a little Spanish*): both mean a small number or amount.
explanation in Latvian: *a few* lieto ar daudzskaitļa lietvārdiem (*a few words, a few shops*), *a little* ar neskaitāmiem lietvārdiem (*a little Spanish*).

task: Say it another way with *a few* or *a little*: There are three or four cafés near my office.
correct answer: There are a few cafés near my office. | Near my office there are a few cafés. | There are a few cafes near my office. | Near my office there are a few cafes. | A few cafés are near my office. | A few cafes are near my office.
explanation shown to learner: *a few* + plural noun (*a few words, a few shops*), *a little* + uncountable noun (*a little Spanish*): both mean a small number or amount.
explanation in Latvian: *a few* lieto ar daudzskaitļa lietvārdiem (*a few words, a few shops*), *a little* ar neskaitāmiem lietvārdiem (*a little Spanish*).

task: Choose the correct option: I need ___ help with my laptop.
explanation shown to learner: *help* is uncountable, so *a little help*. *a few* goes with plural nouns: *a few days*. No *of* here: not *a little of help*.
explanation in Latvian: *help* ir neskaitāms lietvārds, tāpēc *a little help*. *a few* lieto ar daudzskaitļa lietvārdiem: *a few days*. Šeit nelieto *of*: nevis *a little of help*.

task: Correct the mistake. Change one word: There's a few snow on the roads today.
correct answer: There's a little snow on the roads today. | There is a little snow on the roads today. | Today There's a little snow on the roads. | Today there is a little snow on the roads.
explanation shown to learner: *snow* is uncountable, so *a little snow*, not *a few snow*. *a few* goes with plural nouns: *a few cars*.
explanation in Latvian: *snow* ir neskaitāms lietvārds, tāpēc *a little snow*, nevis *a few snow*. *a few* lieto ar daudzskaitļa lietvārdiem: *a few cars*.

task: Which sentence has a mistake?
correct answer: I ordered a pizza. A pizza was cold.
wrong options / checks: My aunt is an engineer in Riga. | I never drink coffee after six. | The sun is very strong today.
explanation shown to learner: The second time we talk about the pizza, both people know which one: *I ordered a pizza. The pizza was cold.*
explanation in Latvian: Otrajā reizē abi zinām, kurš ēdiens domāts: *I ordered a pizza.* *The pizza was cold.*

task: There was ___ wallet on my seat on the bus. ___ wallet was empty.
explanation shown to learner: *a / an* the first time we talk about something; *the* the second time, when we both know which one.
explanation in Latvian: *a / an* lieto, kad par kaut ko runā pirmajā reizē; *the* lieto otrajā reizē, kad abi jau zinām, kurš tas ir.

task: Complete with *a*, *an* or *the*: My sister has ___ new job. ___ job is in Riga.
explanation shown to learner: *a / an* the first time we talk about something; *the* the second time, when we both know which one.
explanation in Latvian: *a / an* lieto, kad par kaut ko runā pirmajā reizē; *the* lieto otrajā reizē, kad abi jau zinām, kurš tas ir.

task: Complete with *a*, *an* or *the*: We rented ___ car in Spain. ___ car was very small.
explanation shown to learner: *a / an* the first time we talk about something; *the* the second time, when we both know which one.
explanation in Latvian: *a / an* lieto, kad par kaut ko runā pirmajā reizē; *the* lieto otrajā reizē, kad abi jau zinām, kurš tas ir.

task: Correct the mistake: I bought a new laptop. A laptop is very fast.
correct answer: I bought a new laptop. The laptop is very fast. | I bought a new laptop. It is very fast. | I bought a new laptop. It's very fast.
explanation shown to learner: We already know which laptop (the new one), so the second time it is *the laptop* (or *it*).
explanation in Latvian: Mēs jau zinām, kurš klēpjdators domāts, tāpēc otrajā reizē ir *the laptop* (vai *it*).

topic: Prepositions of time and place (in, on, at)
task: Which sentence has a mistake?
correct answer: I started a new job on last Monday.
wrong options / checks: The shop opens at nine. | We often go skiing in February. | My birthday is on 3 June.
explanation shown to learner: No preposition before *last / next / this / every*: *I started a new job last Monday.* But *on Monday* without *last*.
explanation in Latvian: Pirms *last / next / this / every* prievārdu nelieto: *I started a new job last Monday.* Bet *on Monday* bez *last*.

topic: Prepositions of time and place (in, on, at)
task: Choose the correct option: Are you free ___ this weekend?
explanation shown to learner: With *this* there is no preposition: *this weekend*. Without *this* we say *at the weekend*.
explanation in Latvian: Ar *this* prievārdu nelieto: *this weekend*. Bez *this* saka *at the weekend*.

topic: Prepositions of time and place (in, on, at)
task: I check my email ___ every morning.
explanation shown to learner: With *every* there is no preposition: *every morning*. Without *every* we say *in the morning*.
explanation in Latvian: Ar *every* prievārdu nelieto: *every morning*. Bez *every* saka *in the morning*.

topic: Prepositions of time and place (in, on, at)
task: The new gym opens ___ tomorrow.
explanation shown to learner: No preposition before *tomorrow* and *yesterday*: *The gym opens tomorrow.*
explanation in Latvian: Pirms *tomorrow* un *yesterday* prievārdu nelieto: *The gym opens tomorrow.*

topic: Prepositions of time and place (in, on, at)
task: Correct the mistake: We arrived in Rome on yesterday.
correct answer: We arrived in Rome yesterday. | Yesterday we arrived in Rome.
explanation shown to learner: No preposition before *yesterday* and *tomorrow*: *We arrived in Rome yesterday.*
explanation in Latvian: Pirms *yesterday* un *tomorrow* prievārdu nelieto: *We arrived in Rome yesterday.*

task: Write *a*, *an* or *some*: I need ___ umbrella and ___ money.
explanation shown to learner: *umbrella* is one thing we can count, so *an* (it starts with a vowel sound). *money* is uncountable: *some money*, never *a money*.
explanation in Latvian: *umbrella* ir skaitāms lietvārds, tāpēc *an* (sākas ar patskaņa skaņu). *money* ir neskaitāms lietvārds: *some money*, nekad *a money*.

task: Which sentence has a mistake?
correct answer: I don't have some free time this week.
wrong options / checks: I'd like a sandwich and some water. | Are there any shops near your hotel? | Our office has some new computers.
explanation shown to learner: In a negative sentence we use *any*, not *some*: *I don't have any free time this week.* *some* is for positive sentences, *any* for negatives and questions.
explanation in Latvian: Noliegumā lieto *any*, nevis *some*: *I don't have any free time this week.* *some* lieto apgalvojumā, *any* noliegumā un jautājumā.

task: Write *a*, *some* or *any*: There's ___ toaster, but there isn't ___ bread.
explanation shown to learner: *toaster* is one thing we can count: *a toaster*. *bread* is uncountable, and in a negative sentence we use *any*: *there isn't any bread*, never *a bread*.
explanation in Latvian: *toaster* ir skaitāms lietvārds: *a toaster*. *bread* ir neskaitāms lietvārds, un noliegumā lieto *any*: *there isn't any bread*, nekad *a bread*.

task: Make a yes/no question: There are some yoga classes on Sunday.
correct answer: Are there any yoga classes on Sunday? | Are there any yoga classes on Sundays? | Are there yoga classes on Sunday? | Are there yoga classes on Sundays? | Are there some yoga classes on Sunday? | Are there some yoga classes on Sundays?
explanation shown to learner: In a question we usually use *any*, not *some*: *Are there any yoga classes on Sunday?* *some* is for positive sentences.
explanation in Latvian: Jautājumā parasti lieto *any*, nevis *some*: *Are there any yoga classes on Sunday?* *some* lieto apgalvojumā.
answer notes: Are there some yoga classes on Sunday? :: Correct too when you expect the answer *yes*. A plain question, when you don't know, usually has *any*: *Are there any yoga classes on Sunday?* :: Arī pareizi, ja gaidi atbildi *yes*. Parastā jautājumā, kad nezini, parasti lieto *any*: *Are there any yoga classes on Sunday?*

task: Choose the correct option: The office is empty. Everyone ___ home.
explanation shown to learner: The person is not here now, so *gone*: *has / have gone* = went and is still there. *been* would mean they are back. After *have / has* use the 3rd form, not *went*.
explanation in Latvian: Cilvēks tagad nav šeit, tāpēc *gone*: *has / have gone* = aizgāja un vēl ir tur. *been* nozīmētu, ka viņš jau ir atpakaļ. Aiz *have / has* lieto 3. formu, nevis *went*.

task: Choose the correct option: I've ___ to the gym. I feel great now.
explanation shown to learner: The person is back (or is here and speaking), so *been*: *have / has been to* = went and came back. *gone* would mean they are still there. After *have / has* use the 3rd form, not *went*.
explanation in Latvian: Cilvēks ir atpakaļ (vai ir šeit un runā), tāpēc *been*: *have / has been to* = aizgāja un atgriezās. *gone* nozīmētu, ka viņš vēl ir tur. Aiz *have / has* lieto 3. formu, nevis *went*.

task: Which sentence has a mistake?
correct answer: My parents have gone to Italy twice.
wrong options / checks: Have you ever been to a jazz concert? | Ivo has gone home. He felt ill. | I haven't seen my cousin this year.
explanation shown to learner: Visits that are over can be counted (*twice, three times*): *My parents have been to Italy twice.* *gone* means they are still there, so it cannot happen twice.
explanation in Latvian: Apmeklējumus, kas jau beigušies, var saskaitīt (*twice, three times*): *My parents have been to Italy twice.* *gone* nozīmē, ka viņi vēl ir tur, tāpēc ar *twice* jālieto *been*.

task: Write *been* or *gone*: We have ___ to the cinema twice this month.
explanation shown to learner: *twice* counts visits that are over: we went and came back, so *been*.
explanation in Latvian: *twice* norāda uz apmeklējumiem, kas jau beigušies: aizgājām un atgriezāmies, tāpēc *been*.

task: Write *been* or *gone*: Dan's ___ to a football match. He'll be back at ten.
explanation shown to learner: He is not back yet (*He'll be back at ten*), so he is still at the match: *gone*.
explanation in Latvian: Viņš vēl nav atpakaļ (*He'll be back at ten*), tātad viņš vēl ir mačā: *gone*.

task: Where's Oskars? He ___ ___ to the airport to meet his parents.
explanation shown to learner: The person is not here now, so *gone*: *has / have gone* = went and is still there. *been* would mean they are back. After *have / has* use the 3rd form, not *went*.
explanation in Latvian: Cilvēks tagad nav šeit, tāpēc *gone*: *has / have gone* = aizgāja un vēl ir tur. *been* nozīmētu, ka viņš jau ir atpakaļ. Aiz *have / has* lieto 3. formu, nevis *went*.

task: Your car looks so clean! Have you ___ to the car wash?
explanation shown to learner: The person is back (or is here and speaking), so *been*: *have / has been to* = went and came back. *gone* would mean they are still there. After *have / has* use the 3rd form, not *went*.
explanation in Latvian: Cilvēks ir atpakaļ (vai ir šeit un runā), tāpēc *been*: *have / has been to* = aizgāja un atgriezās. *gone* nozīmētu, ka viņš vēl ir tur. Aiz *have / has* lieto 3. formu, nevis *went*.

task: I can't call Lena now. She's ___ to bed.
explanation shown to learner: The person is not here now, so *gone*: *has / have gone* = went and is still there. *been* would mean they are back. After *have / has* use the 3rd form, not *went*.
explanation in Latvian: Cilvēks tagad nav šeit, tāpēc *gone*: *has / have gone* = aizgāja un vēl ir tur. *been* nozīmētu, ka viņš jau ir atpakaļ. Aiz *have / has* lieto 3. formu, nevis *went*.

task: Our friends are back from their holiday. They ___ ___ to Greece.
explanation shown to learner: The person is back (or is here and speaking), so *been*: *have / has been to* = went and came back. *gone* would mean they are still there. After *have / has* use the 3rd form, not *went*.
explanation in Latvian: Cilvēks ir atpakaļ (vai ir šeit un runā), tāpēc *been*: *have / has been to* = aizgāja un atgriezās. *gone* nozīmētu, ka viņš vēl ir tur. Aiz *have / has* lieto 3. formu, nevis *went*.

task: Start with *Rita has* and use *go*: Rita went to Tokyo, and she is still there.
correct answer: Rita has gone to Tokyo. | Rita has gone to Tokyo, and she is still there. | Rita has gone to Tokyo and is still there.
explanation shown to learner: She went and is still there: *has gone to*. *has been to* would mean she is back.
explanation in Latvian: Viņa aizgāja un vēl ir tur: *has gone to*. *has been to* nozīmētu, ka viņa ir atpakaļ.

task: Choose the correct option: I have ___ for you!
wrong options / checks: a good news | a good new
explanation shown to learner: *news* is uncountable and always ends in *-s*: *some good news*, *the news*, never *a news* or *a new*.
explanation in Latvian: *news* ir neskaitāms lietvārds un vienmēr beidzas ar *-s*: *some good news, the news*, nekad *a news* vai *a new*. Tulkojot burtiski, laba ziņa dod *a good news*.

task: I found ___ useful ___ on this website.
explanation shown to learner: *advice, information, furniture, news, luggage* are uncountable: no *a / an*, no plural *-s*, and a singular verb: *some news, The furniture is new.*
explanation in Latvian: *advice, information, furniture, news, luggage* ir neskaitāmi lietvārdi: bez *a / an*, bez daudzskaitļa *-s*, un darbības vārds vienskaitlī: *some news, The furniture is new*.

task: Which sentence has a mistake?
correct answer: My boss gave me a useful advice.
wrong options / checks: Our new furniture is very comfortable. | We haven't got much luggage. | Can I ask you for some information?
explanation shown to learner: *advice* is uncountable: *some advice*, *a piece of advice*, never *an advice* or *advices*; the verb is singular: *Your advice is…*
explanation in Latvian: *advice* ir neskaitāms lietvārds: *some advice, a piece of advice*, nekad *an advice* vai *advices*; darbības vārds vienskaitlī: *Your advice is*… Tulkojot burtiski, latviešu padoms, padomi dod *an advice, advices*.

task: Put the words in order to make a question.
correct answer: can i give you a piece of advice
explanation shown to learner: To count an uncountable noun, use *a piece of / two pieces of*: *a piece of advice*, *How many pieces of luggage?* In a question the helping verb (or *am / is / are*) goes before the subject.
explanation in Latvian: Lai saskaitītu neskaitāmu lietvārdu, lieto *a piece of / two pieces of*: *a piece of advice, How many pieces of luggage*? Jautājumā palīgdarbības vārds (vai *am / is / are*) stāv pirms teikuma priekšmeta.

task: My ___ ___ still at the airport.
explanation shown to learner: An uncountable noun takes a singular verb: *is*, *has*, verb + *-s*. *luggage* has no plural: *My luggage is …*
explanation in Latvian: Neskaitāmam lietvārdam darbības vārds ir vienskaitlī: *is, has*, darbības vārds + *-s*. *luggage* nav daudzskaitļa: *My luggage is* …

task: Choose the correct option: We need ___ for our new office.
explanation shown to learner: *advice, information, furniture, news, luggage* are uncountable: no *a / an*, no plural *-s*, and a singular verb: *some news, The furniture is new.*
explanation in Latvian: *advice, information, furniture, news, luggage* ir neskaitāmi lietvārdi: bez *a / an*, bez daudzskaitļa *-s*, un darbības vārds vienskaitlī: *some news, The furniture is new*.

task: Thank you! Your advice about the exam ___ really helpful. (be)
correct answer: is | was | has been | will be | 's
explanation shown to learner: *advice* is uncountable: *some advice*, *a piece of advice*, never *an advice* or *advices*; the verb is singular: *Your advice is…*
explanation in Latvian: *advice* ir neskaitāms lietvārds: *some advice, a piece of advice*, nekad *an advice* vai *advices*; darbības vārds vienskaitlī: *Your advice is*… Tulkojot burtiski, latviešu padoms, padomi dod *an advice, advices*.

task: Put the words in order to make a question.
correct answer: how many pieces of luggage do you have
explanation shown to learner: To count an uncountable noun, use *a piece of / two pieces of*: *a piece of advice*, *How many pieces of luggage?*
explanation in Latvian: Lai saskaitītu neskaitāmu lietvārdu, lieto *a piece of / two pieces of*: *a piece of advice, How many pieces of luggage*?

task: Rewrite with *furniture*: The chairs and tables in this café are new.
correct answer: The furniture in this café is new. | The furniture in this café is all new. | All the furniture in this café is new. | All of the furniture in this café is new. | The furniture in the café is new. | This café's furniture is new. | The café's furniture is new. | This café has new furniture. | The café has new furniture.
explanation shown to learner: *furniture* (chairs, tables, beds…) is uncountable: no plural, and a singular verb: *The furniture is new.*
explanation in Latvian: *furniture* (mēbeles) ir neskaitāms lietvārds: bez daudzskaitļa, un darbības vārds vienskaitlī: *The furniture is new.* Tulkojot burtiski, mēbeles ir dod *furnitures are*.

topic: Prepositions of time and place (in, on, at)
task: Choose the correct option: We arrived ___ the hotel after midnight.
explanation shown to learner: *arrive at* + a place such as a hotel, a station or a cinema; *arrive in* + a city or country. Never *arrive to*.
explanation in Latvian: *arrive at* + konkrēta vieta, piemēram, viesnīca; *arrive in* lieto ar pilsētām un valstīm. Nekad *arrive to*. Tulkojot burtiski ieradāmies uz viesnīcu, sanāk kļūda *arrived to*.

topic: Prepositions of time and place (in, on, at)
task: Choose the correct option: What time did you ___ the office today?
explanation shown to learner: *get to* + a place = arrive there: *What time did you get to the office?* *arrive* needs *at*: *arrive at the office*.
explanation in Latvian: *get to* + vieta = nokļūt: *What time did you get to the office?* Ar *arrive* vajag *at*: *arrive at the office*.

topic: Prepositions of time and place (in, on, at)
task: Which sentence has a mistake?
correct answer: We arrived to Oslo late on Friday.
wrong options / checks: She ran into the kitchen. | The road goes through the forest. | I walk past your house every day.
explanation shown to learner: *arrive in* + a city or country: *We arrived in Oslo.* Never *arrive to*.
explanation in Latvian: *arrive in* lieto ar pilsētām un valstīm: *We arrived in Oslo.* Tulkojot burtiski atbraucām uz Norvēģiju, sanāk kļūda *arrived to*.

topic: Prepositions of time and place (in, on, at)
task: Choose the correct option: Walk ___ the bank and turn left.
explanation shown to learner: *past* = going by something without stopping: *Walk past the bank.* *passed* is the past of the verb *pass*.
explanation in Latvian: *past* = garām: *Walk past the bank.* *passed* ir darbības vārda *pass* pagātnes forma.

topic: Prepositions of time and place (in, on, at)
task: Put the words in order.
correct answer: let's walk along the beach after lunch
wrong options / checks: also accepted: after lunch let's walk along the beach
explanation shown to learner: *along* = following a line such as a river, a road or a beach: *walk along the beach*.
explanation in Latvian: *along* = pa: *walk along the beach*.

topic: Prepositions of time and place (in, on, at)
task: We swam ___ the river to the other side.
explanation shown to learner: *across* = from one side to the other: *swim across the river*.
explanation in Latvian: *across* = pāri: *swim across the river*.

topic: Prepositions of time and place (in, on, at)
task: The cat came in ___ the open window.
explanation shown to learner: *through* = in at one side and out at the other of something with sides or an opening: *through the window, through the tunnel*.
explanation in Latvian: *through* = caur, cauri: *through the window, through the tunnel*.

topic: Prepositions of time and place (in, on, at)
task: Write one word in each gap: At airport security, take your laptop ___ ___ your bag.
explanation shown to learner: *out of* = from inside to outside: *take your laptop out of your bag*. Opposite: *into*.
explanation in Latvian: *out of* = no iekšienes ārā: *take your laptop out of your bag*. Pretējais: *into*.

topic: Prepositions of time and place (in, on, at)
task: Correct the mistake: What time did you get to home last night?
correct answer: What time did you get home last night? | What time did you arrive home last night? | What time did you get to your home last night?
explanation shown to learner: *go home, get home, come home*: no *to* before *home*.
explanation in Latvian: *go home, get home, come home*: pirms *home* nelieto to. Tulkojot burtiski nokļuvi uz mājām, sanāk kļūda *get to home*.
answer notes: What time did you get to your home last night? :: Correct: with *your* before it, *home* is an ordinary noun and takes *get to*. But we usually say *get home*, with no *to* and no *your*. :: Pareizi: ar *your* priekšā *home* ir parasts lietvārds, un tad lieto *get to*. Tomēr parasti saka *get home*, bez *to* un bez *your*.

task: Choose the correct option: We enjoyed the cooking class ___.
explanation shown to learner: *very much* goes at the end, after the verb and its object: *We enjoyed the class very much.* Not *very* or *much* alone, and not *much very*.
explanation in Latvian: *very much* ir teikuma beigās, aiz darbības vārda un tā papildinātāja: *We enjoyed the class very much.* Nevis *very, much* vai *much very*.

task: Which sentence has a mistake?
wrong options / checks: The hotel was quite small. | My boss speaks really fast. | This soup is too salty.
explanation shown to learner: *very* goes before an adjective or an adverb (*very good, very fast*), never before a verb. With a verb: *I really like it* or *I like it very much*.
explanation in Latvian: Tulkojot burtiski ļoti patīk, sanāk *I very like it.* Angliski *very* liek pirms īpašības vārda vai apstākļa vārda (*very good*); ar darbības vārdu saka *I really like it* vai *I like it very much.*

task: Put the words in order.
correct answer: i like my new flat very much
wrong options / checks: also accepted: i very much like my new flat
explanation shown to learner: *very much* goes at the end, after the verb and its object: *We enjoyed the class very much.* Not *very* or *much* alone, and not *much very*.
explanation in Latvian: *very much* ir teikuma beigās, aiz darbības vārda un tā papildinātāja: *We enjoyed the class very much.* Nevis *very, much* vai *much very*.

task: This suitcase is ___ heavy for me.
wrong options / checks: bank: too | too much | very much
explanation shown to learner: *too* + adjective = more than is good: *too heavy*. Not *too much heavy* or *very much heavy*; *too much* goes with a noun (*too much luggage*).
explanation in Latvian: *too* + īpašības vārds = vairāk, nekā vajag: *too heavy*. Nevis *too much heavy* vai *very much heavy; too much* lieto ar lietvārdu (*too much luggage*).

task: Complete with one word: My grandmother loves her garden very ___.
explanation shown to learner: *very much* goes at the end, after the verb and its object: *We enjoyed the class very much.* Not *very* or *much* alone, and not *much very*.
explanation in Latvian: *very much* ir teikuma beigās, aiz darbības vārda un tā papildinātāja: *We enjoyed the class very much.* Nevis *very, much* vai *much very*.

task: Put the words in order.
correct answer: we had a very nice holiday
explanation shown to learner: A degree word goes right before the adjective: *a very nice holiday*, *really good*, *quite small*.
explanation in Latvian: Pakāpes apstākļa vārds ir tieši pirms īpašības vārda: *a very nice holiday, really good, quite small*.

task: I ___ like this podcast.
explanation shown to learner: *very* goes before an adjective or an adverb (*very good, very fast*), never before a verb. With a verb: *I really like it* or *I like it very much*.
explanation in Latvian: Tulkojot burtiski ļoti patīk, sanāk *I very like it.* Angliski *very* liek pirms īpašības vārda vai apstākļa vārda (*very good*); ar darbības vārdu saka *I really like it* vai *I like it very much.*

task: Say it another way with *really*: We liked the new restaurant very much.
correct answer: We really liked the new restaurant.
explanation shown to learner: *very* goes before an adjective or an adverb (*very good, very fast*), never before a verb. With a verb: *I really like it* or *I like it very much*.
explanation in Latvian: Tulkojot burtiski ļoti patīk, sanāk *I very like it.* Angliski *very* liek pirms īpašības vārda vai apstākļa vārda (*very good*); ar darbības vārdu saka *I really like it* vai *I like it very much.*

topic: Comparison: -er, more, the most, as ... as
task: Choose the correct option: Please drive ___. The road is icy.
wrong options / checks: slowlier | more slowlier | the most slowly
explanation shown to learner: *slowly* has *-ly*, so the comparative is *more slowly* (*slower* is also heard in everyday speech). Not *slowlier* or *more slowlier*; *the most slowly* compares with a whole group.
explanation in Latvian: *slowly* beidzas ar *-ly*, tāpēc pārākā pakāpe ir *more slowly* (sarunvalodā dzird arī *slower*). Nevis *slowlier* vai *more slowlier; the most slowly* salīdzina ar visu grupu.

topic: Comparison: -er, more, the most, as ... as
task: Which sentence has a mistake?
correct answer: Tom drives more fast than his father.
wrong options / checks: We arrived later than the others. | My new phone charges much faster. | Who sings the best in your family?
explanation shown to learner: *fast* has no *-ly*: the comparative is *faster*, not *more fast*: *Tom drives faster than his father.* The other three are correct: *later than*, *much faster*, *the best*.
explanation in Latvian: *fast* nav *-ly* galotnes: pārākā pakāpe ir *faster*, nevis *more fast*: *Tom drives faster than his father.* Pārējie trīs teikumi ir pareizi: *later than, much faster, the best*.

topic: Comparison: -er, more, the most, as ... as
task: Put the words in order.
correct answer: my sister speaks english more fluently than me
explanation shown to learner: The adverb comes after the verb and its object: *speaks English more fluently*, then *than* + the other person (*than me*). Not *speaks more fluently English*.
explanation in Latvian: Apstākļa vārds nāk aiz darbības vārda un tā papildinātāja: *speaks English more fluently*, tad *than* + otrs cilvēks (*than me*). Nevis *speaks more fluently English*. Tulkojot burtiski "runā brīvāk angliski", sanāk *speaks more fluently English*.

topic: Comparison: -er, more, the most, as ... as
task: She plays the guitar ___ than her brother.
explanation shown to learner: *well* and *badly* are irregular: *well → better → the best*, *badly → worse → the worst*. Not *more well* or *more good*.
explanation in Latvian: *well* un *badly* ir nekārtni: *well → better → the best, badly → worse → the worst*. Nevis *more well* vai *more good*.

topic: Comparison: -er, more, the most, as ... as
task: Marta has never had an accident. She drives ___ than her brother. (careful)
correct answer: more carefully | much more carefully | a lot more carefully | far more carefully
explanation shown to learner: *drive* needs an adverb: *careful → carefully*, and with *-ly* the comparative is *more carefully*. Not *more careful* (that is the adjective).
explanation in Latvian: Aiz *drive* vajag apstākļa vārdu: *careful → carefully*, un ar *-ly* pārākā pakāpe ir *more carefully*. Nevis *more careful* (tas ir īpašības vārds).

topic: Comparison: -er, more, the most, as ... as
task: Today I started work ___ than usual. (early)
correct answer: earlier | much earlier | a bit earlier | a lot earlier
explanation shown to learner: *early* is an adverb and an adjective: *early → earlier* (*y → i* + *-er*). Not *more early*.
explanation in Latvian: *early* ir apstākļa vārds un arī īpašības vārds: *early → earlier* (*y → i + -er*). Nevis *more early*.

topic: Comparison: -er, more, the most, as ... as
task: Of all my colleagues, Anna lives ___ from the office. (far)
correct answer: the furthest | the farthest | furthest | farthest
explanation shown to learner: *Of all* compares one person with the whole group: superlative. *far* is irregular: *far → further → the furthest* (*farther, the farthest* are correct too). With an adverb, *the* is often left out.
explanation in Latvian: *Of all* salīdzina vienu cilvēku ar visu grupu: vispārākā pakāpe. *far* ir nekārtns: *far → further → the furthest* (der arī *farther, the farthest*). Ar apstākļa vārdu *the* bieži izlaiž.

topic: Comparison: -er, more, the most, as ... as
task: Start with *My brother*: I cook worse than my brother.
correct answer: My brother cooks better than me. | My brother cooks better than I do. | My brother cooks better than I. | My brother cooks better than I cook. | My brother cooks much better than me. | My brother cooks much better than I do. | My brother cooks a lot better than me. | My brother cooks a lot better than I do. | My brother is a better cook than me. | My brother is a better cook than I am. | My brother is a better cook than I.
explanation shown to learner: *well* and *badly* are irregular: *well → better → the best*, *badly → worse → the worst*. Not *more well* or *more good*.
explanation in Latvian: *well* un *badly* ir nekārtni: *well → better → the best, badly → worse → the worst*. Nevis *more well* vai *more good*.

task: Choose the correct option: It was very hot, so I ___ sleep last night.
explanation shown to learner: Past: *couldn't* + base verb. *can't* is the present, and *could* never goes with *did / didn't*.
explanation in Latvian: Pagātnē: *couldn't* + pamatforma. *can't* ir tagadne, un *could* nekad nelieto ar *did / didn't*.

task: Which sentence has a mistake?
correct answer: When I was ten, I can speak French.
wrong options / checks: We couldn't find a taxi at the airport. | My first phone could only make calls. | Could you cook when you were a student?
explanation shown to learner: *When I was ten* is the past: *I could speak French*, not *I can*.
explanation in Latvian: *When I was ten* ir pagātne: *I could speak French*, nevis *I can.*

task: Put the words in order.
correct answer: we couldn't see the stage from our seats
wrong options / checks: also accepted: from our seats we couldn't see the stage
explanation shown to learner: Past: *couldn't* + base verb. *can't* is the present, and *could* never goes with *did / didn't*.
explanation in Latvian: Pagātnē: *couldn't* + pamatforma. *can't* ir tagadne, un *could* nekad nelieto ar *did / didn't*.

task: Put the words in order.
correct answer: when i was younger i could run much faster
wrong options / checks: also accepted: i could run much faster when i was younger
explanation shown to learner: Ability in the past: *could* + base verb (no *to*, no past form): *I could read at four.*
explanation in Latvian: Spēja pagātnē: *could* + darbības vārda pamatforma (bez to, bez pagātnes formas): *I could read at four.*

task: ___ your parents ___ a car when they were young?
explanation shown to learner: Question about the past: *Could* + subject + base verb? No *did*: *Could you swim at six?*
explanation in Latvian: Jautājums par pagātni: *Could* + teik. priekšmets + pamatforma? Bez *did*: *Could you swim at six?*

task: As a teenager, Ben ___ ___ any song on the guitar.
explanation shown to learner: Ability in the past: *could* + base verb (no *to*, no past form): *I could read at four.*
explanation in Latvian: Spēja pagātnē: *could* + darbības vārda pamatforma (bez to, bez pagātnes formas): *I could read at four.*

task: Make a yes/no question: Tom could speak German when he lived in Berlin.
correct answer: Could Tom speak German when he lived in Berlin? | When he lived in Berlin, could Tom speak German? | Was Tom able to speak German when he lived in Berlin? | When he lived in Berlin, was Tom able to speak German?
explanation shown to learner: Question about the past: *Could* + subject + base verb? No *did*: *Could you swim at six?*
explanation in Latvian: Jautājums par pagātni: *Could* + teik. priekšmets + pamatforma? Bez *did*: *Could you swim at six?*

task: Choose the correct option: The party was great. ___ had a good time.
explanation shown to learner: *every-* = all the people: *Everybody had a good time.* *any-* is for questions and negatives, and *Nobody* would mean that no person had a good time.
explanation in Latvian: *every*- = visi cilvēki: *Everybody had a good time.* *any*- lieto jautājumos un noliegumos, bet *Nobody* nozīmētu, ka neviens nav labi pavadījis laiku.

task: Which sentence has a mistake?
correct answer: I heard anybody in the garden last night.
wrong options / checks: Did anyone call me this morning? | Everybody in my office drives to work. | Nobody in my family can cook.
explanation shown to learner: In a positive sentence use *some-*: *I heard somebody in the garden.* *any-* is for questions and negatives. The other three are correct: *Did anyone…?* (a question), *Everybody … drives* (all the people), *Nobody … can cook* (*no-* with a positive verb).
explanation in Latvian: Apgalvojumā lieto *some*-: *I heard somebody in the garden.* *any*- lieto jautājumos un noliegumos. Pārējie trīs ir pareizi: *Did anyone*…? (jautājums), *Everybody* … *drives* (visi cilvēki), *Nobody* … *can cook* (*Nobody* ar apgalvojuma formu).

task: My glasses are ___ in this room. Can you help me look?
explanation shown to learner: A place we don't know, in a positive sentence: *somewhere*. *anywhere* is for questions and negatives; *something* is a thing, not a place.
explanation in Latvian: Vieta, ko nezinām, apgalvojumā: *somewhere*. *anywhere* lieto jautājumos un noliegumos; *something* ir lieta, nevis vieta.

task: There's ___ in my wallet. It's empty.
explanation shown to learner: *There's* is a positive verb, so the word itself says no: *There's nothing in my wallet.* *anything* needs a negative (*There isn't anything*); *something* does not fit an empty wallet.
explanation in Latvian: *There's* ir apgalvojuma forma, tāpēc noliegumu izsaka pats vārds: *There's nothing in my wallet.* *anything* vajag noliegumu (*There isn't anything*); *something* neder tukšam makam.

task: Complete with a word like *someone, anything, nowhere*: ___ works here on Sundays. The office is closed.
explanation shown to learner: *Nobody / No one* already makes the sentence negative, so the verb stays positive: *Nobody works here on Sundays.*
explanation in Latvian: *Nobody* jau ir noliegums, tāpēc darbības vārds paliek apgalvojumā: *Nobody works here on Sundays.*
replaces: ___ works here on Sundays. The office is closed.

task: Complete with a word like *someone, anything, nowhere*: There are trees ___: in the streets, in the parks, by the river.
explanation shown to learner: *every-* = all: *everywhere* = in all places. The list after the colon shows that the trees are in all the places.
explanation in Latvian: *every*- = visi: *everywhere* = visur, visās vietās. Uzskaitījums aiz kola rāda, ka koki ir visās vietās.
replaces: There are trees ___: in the streets, in the parks, by the river.

task: Make it negative: I bought something for Anna.
correct answer: I didn't buy anything for Anna. | I didn't buy Anna anything. | I bought nothing for Anna.
explanation shown to learner: In a negative sentence *something* becomes *anything*: *I didn't buy anything for Anna.* With a positive verb, *nothing* says the same: *I bought nothing for Anna.*
explanation in Latvian: Noliegumā *something* kļūst par *anything*: *I didn't buy anything for Anna.* Ar apgalvojuma formu to pašu saka *nothing*: *I bought nothing for Anna.*

task: Choose the correct option: My sister loves swimming and ___.
explanation shown to learner: After *and* / *or* use the same form as before it: *swimming and cycling*, *-ing and -ing*.
explanation in Latvian: Aiz *and / or* lieto to pašu formu, kas ir pirms tā, piemēram, *swimming and cycling*.

task: Which sentence has a mistake?
correct answer: I usually have breakfast and reading the news.
wrong options / checks: It was raining, so we took a taxi home. | I'm tired today because I slept badly. | Is the meeting today or tomorrow morning?
explanation shown to learner: With *and* we need not say the subject again, but the second verb has the same form as the first: *I have breakfast and read the news*, *we visited … and worked*.
explanation in Latvian: Ar *and* teikuma priekšmetu var neatkārtot, bet otrais darbības vārds ir tādā pašā formā kā pirmais: *I have breakfast and read the news.* Arī *we visited* … *and worked*.

task: Would you like to stay in tonight or ___ out?
explanation shown to learner: *would like to stay in or go out*: after *or* the same form as before it (*to*) *stay* → *go*; *to* need not be repeated. Not *going*.
explanation in Latvian: *would like to stay in or go out*: aiz *or* tā pati forma kā pirms tā: *stay*, tātad *go*. *to* var neatkārtot. Nevis *going*.

task: On Saturday we visited my parents and ___ in their garden.
explanation shown to learner: With *and* we need not say the subject again, but the second verb has the same form as the first: *I have breakfast and read the news*, *we visited … and worked*.
explanation in Latvian: Ar *and* teikuma priekšmetu var neatkārtot, bet otrais darbības vārds ir tādā pašā formā kā pirmais: *I have breakfast and read the news.* Arī *we visited* … *and worked*.

task: Thanks for coming and ___ me with the move. (help)
explanation shown to learner: After *for* the verb takes *-ing*, and after *and* the same form again: *for coming and helping*.
explanation in Latvian: Aiz *for* darbības vārds ir ar *-ing*, un aiz *and* jālieto tā pati forma: *for coming and helping*.

task: The best parts of my job are meeting people and ___. (travel)
explanation shown to learner: After *and* / *or* use the same form as before it: *swimming and cycling*, *-ing and -ing*.
explanation in Latvian: Aiz *and / or* lieto to pašu formu, kas ir pirms tā, piemēram, *swimming and cycling*.

task: Correct the mistake: She closed her laptop and go home.
correct answer: She closed her laptop and went home. | She closed her laptop and she went home. | She closes her laptop and goes home. | She closes her laptop and she goes home.
explanation shown to learner: Both verbs after *she* have the same form: *closed … and went* (or *closes … and goes*). The subject need not be repeated after *and*.
explanation in Latvian: Abos darbības vārdos ir tā pati forma: *closed* … *and went* (vai *closes* … *and goes*). Aiz *and* teikuma priekšmetu var neatkārtot.

topic: Prepositions of time and place (in, on, at)
task: Choose the correct option: Is it cheaper to travel to Tallinn ___ bus?
explanation shown to learner: *by* + a kind of transport, with no *a / the / my*: *by bus, by car, by train*. Not *with bus*.
explanation in Latvian: *by* + transportlīdzeklis bez *a / the / my*: *by bus, by car, by train*. Latviski ar autobusu, bet angliski *by bus*, nevis *with bus*.

topic: Prepositions of time and place (in, on, at)
task: Which sentence has a mistake?
correct answer: My daughter goes to school by foot.
wrong options / checks: We travelled around Italy by train. | I fell asleep on the plane. | He picked me up in his car.
explanation shown to learner: Walking is *on foot*, not *by foot*: *We went there on foot.*
explanation in Latvian: Kājām = *on foot*, nevis *by foot*: *We went there on foot.*

topic: Prepositions of time and place (in, on, at)
task: Today I'm going to work ___ Tom's car.
explanation shown to learner: *in* + a car or a taxi: *in a taxi, in my car*. With *a / the / my* in front of the noun, *by* is not possible.
explanation in Latvian: Latviski taksometrā, bet angliski *in a taxi*; tāpat *in my car*. Ja pirms lietvārda ir *a / the / my*, tad *by* nelieto.

topic: Prepositions of time and place (in, on, at)
task: I met an old friend ___ the tram yesterday.
explanation shown to learner: *on* + a bus, train, tram or plane: *on the tram, on the bus*.
explanation in Latvian: Latviski tramvajā, bet angliski *on the tram*; tāpat *on the bus, on the train, on the plane*.

topic: Prepositions of time and place (in, on, at)
task: Write the missing word: Let's go to the museum ___ foot.
explanation shown to learner: Walking is *on foot*, not *by foot*: *We went there on foot.*
explanation in Latvian: Kājām = *on foot*, nevis *by foot*: *We went there on foot.*

topic: Prepositions of time and place (in, on, at)
task: Write the missing word: We went to the airport ___ a taxi.
explanation shown to learner: *in* + a car or a taxi: *in a taxi, in my car*. With *a / the / my* in front of the noun, *by* is not possible.
explanation in Latvian: Latviski taksometrā, bet angliski *in a taxi*; tāpat *in my car*. Ja pirms lietvārda ir *a / the / my*, tad *by* nelieto.

topic: Prepositions of time and place (in, on, at)
task: Correct the mistake: I go to work by my car.
correct answer: I go to work in my car. | I go to work by car.
explanation shown to learner: *by* + transport with no *my*: *by car*. With *my*: *in my car*.
explanation in Latvian: *by* + transportlīdzeklis bez *my*: *by car*. Ar *my*: *in my car*.

task: Choose the correct option: He went to the doctor ___ a check-up.
explanation shown to learner: *for* + noun says what somebody goes somewhere for: *go to the doctor for a check-up*. *to* is followed by a verb (*to have a check-up*).
explanation in Latvian: *for* + lietvārds norāda, pēc kā kāds iet: *go to the doctor for a check-up*. Ar darbības vārdu būtu *to have a check-up*. Kļūda: *to a check-up, on a check-up*.

task: Which sentence has a mistake?
correct answer: I'm learning English for get a better job.
wrong options / checks: She called me to say thank you. | We went to the beach for a swim. | They are staying with us for the weekend.
explanation shown to learner: Before a verb, purpose is *to* + verb: *I'm learning English to get a better job*, not *for get*. *for* comes before a noun: *for a swim*.
explanation in Latvian: Pirms darbības vārda nolūku pauž ar *to get, to buy*: *I'm learning English to get a better job*, nevis *for get*. *for* lieto pirms lietvārda: *for a swim*.

task: Put the words in order.
correct answer: he uses his phone to pay for everything
explanation shown to learner: To say why somebody does something, use *to* + verb: *He uses his phone to pay.* Not *for pay* and not *for paying*.
explanation in Latvian: Kāpēc kāds kaut ko dara, norāda ar *to pay, to get, to stay*: *He uses his phone to pay.* Nevis *for pay* un nevis *for paying*.

task: She goes to the gym ___ ___ fit.
explanation shown to learner: To say why somebody does something, use *to* + verb: *He uses his phone to pay.* Not *for pay* and not *for paying*.
explanation in Latvian: Kāpēc kāds kaut ko dara, norāda ar *to pay, to get, to stay*: *He uses his phone to pay.* Nevis *for pay* un nevis *for paying*.

task: Why did you call the hotel? I called ___ a room. (book)
correct answer: to book | in order to book | so as to book
explanation shown to learner: The answer to *Why?* is *to* + verb: *I called to book a room.* Not *for book* or *for booking*.
explanation in Latvian: Atbilde uz *Why*? ir nolūks ar *to book*: *I called to book a room.* Nevis *for book* vai *for booking*.

task: Join with *to*: I went to the post office. I sent a parcel there.
correct answer: I went to the post office to send a parcel. | I went to the post office to send a parcel there. | I went to the post office in order to send a parcel.
explanation shown to learner: The second sentence says why: *to* + verb, without *I* and without the past form: *I went to the post office to send a parcel.*
explanation in Latvian: Otrais teikums norāda, kāpēc: *to send*, bez *I* un bez pagātnes formas *sent*: *I went to the post office to send a parcel.*

task: Which sentence has a mistake?
correct answer: Our kitchen chairs were made from my uncle.
wrong options / checks: Breakfast is served from seven to ten. | My grandmother was born in a small town. | The museum is visited by thousands of tourists.
explanation shown to learner: The person who did it comes after *by*: *made by my uncle*. *made from* is for the material: *made from wood*.
explanation in Latvian: Cilvēks, kas to izdarīja, nāk aiz *by*: *made by my uncle*. *made from* lieto materiālam: *made from wood*.

task: Complete with one word: Our hotel is owned ___ a Swedish company.
explanation shown to learner: *by* + the doer tells us who does the action: *The hotel is owned by a Swedish company.* Not *from* or *of*.
explanation in Latvian: *by* + darītājs norāda, kurš izdarīja darbību: *The hotel is owned by a Swedish company.* Nevis *from* vai *of*.

task: In our village, the bread is baked ___ a local family.
explanation shown to learner: Who bakes it? A local family, so *by a local family*. *from* is for what it is made of: *baked from rye flour*.
explanation in Latvian: Darītājs ir vietējā ģimene, tāpēc *by a local family*. *from* lieto materiālam: *baked from rye flour*.

task: Write one word in each gap: The windows of our office are ___ ___ a small company every month. (clean)
explanation shown to learner: After *are* the 3rd form: *are cleaned*. The doer comes after *by*: *by a small company*.
explanation in Latvian: Aiz *are* vajag 3. formu: *are cleaned*. Darītājs nāk aiz *by*: *by a small company*.

task: Start with *This bridge*: A Latvian engineer designed this bridge.
correct answer: This bridge was designed by a Latvian engineer.
explanation shown to learner: *This bridge* first, then *was* + 3rd form; the engineer is important here, so *by a Latvian engineer* stays: *This bridge was designed by a Latvian engineer.*
explanation in Latvian: Sākumā *This bridge*, tad *was* + 3. forma; inženieris šeit ir svarīgs, tāpēc *by a Latvian engineer* paliek: *This bridge was designed by a Latvian engineer.*

task: Which sentence has a mistake?
correct answer: My glasses is in the car.
wrong options / checks: These kitchen scissors are very sharp. | My feet hurt after the long walk. | People in this town are very friendly.
explanation shown to learner: *glasses* (for your eyes) is always plural: *My glasses are in the car.* *scissors* too: *are*. *feet* and *people* are plural: *hurt*, *are*.
explanation in Latvian: *glasses* vienmēr ir daudzskaitlī: *My glasses are in the car.* Arī *scissors*: *are*. *feet* un *people* ir daudzskaitlī: *hurt, are*.

task: Can I borrow ___ ___ for a minute?
wrong options / checks: bank: a pair of | a | scissors | scissor
explanation shown to learner: *scissors* is always plural: no *a scissors*, no *a scissor*. To say one, use *a pair of scissors*.
explanation in Latvian: *scissors* vienmēr ir daudzskaitlī: nav *a scissors*, nav *a scissor*. Par vienām šķērēm saka *a pair of scissors*. Tulkojot burtiski, vienas šķēres dod *a scissors*.

task: My jeans ___ too big for me now. (be)
explanation shown to learner: *jeans, trousers, glasses, scissors* are always plural (they have two parts), so the verb is plural: *are*, *have*, verb without *-s*.
explanation in Latvian: *jeans, trousers, glasses, scissors* vienmēr ir daudzskaitlī (tiem ir divas daļas), tāpēc darbības vārds ir daudzskaitlī: *are, have*, darbības vārds bez *-s*.

task: Correct the mistake: Your trousers looks great with that jacket.
correct answer: Your trousers look great with that jacket. | Your pair of trousers looks great with that jacket.
explanation shown to learner: *trousers* is always plural, so the verb has no *-s*: *Your trousers look great*, not *looks*.
explanation in Latvian: *trousers* vienmēr ir daudzskaitlī, tāpēc darbības vārds ir bez *-s*: *Your trousers look great*, nevis *looks*.
answer notes: Your pair of trousers looks great with that jacket. :: Correct too: here the subject is *pair* (one pair), so the verb has *-s*. With *trousers* alone: *Your trousers look great*. :: Arī pareizi: te teikuma priekšmets ir *pair* (viens pāris), tāpēc darbības vārdam ir *-s*. Tikai ar *trousers*: *Your trousers look great*.

task: ___ we had dinner, we went for a walk by the sea.
explanation shown to learner: *after* + subject + verb joins two actions in one sentence: *After we had dinner, we went for a walk.* *Then* and *after that* start a new sentence: *We had dinner. Then we went for a walk.*
explanation in Latvian: *after* + teik. priekšmets + darbības vārds savieno divas darbības vienā teikumā: *After we had dinner, we went for a walk.* *Then* un *after that* stāv nākamā teikuma sākumā: *We had dinner.* *Then we went for a walk.*

task: We always buy popcorn ___ the film.
explanation shown to learner: *before* (and *after*) can come before a noun: *before the film*. *while* and *when* need subject + verb: *while the film is on*, *when the film starts*.
explanation in Latvian: *before* (un *after*) lieto arī pirms lietvārda: *before the film*. Aiz *while* un *when* vajag teik. priekšmetu + darbības vārdu: *while the film is on, when the film starts*.

task: Which sentence has a mistake?
correct answer: Before go to work, I walk the dog.
wrong options / checks: We had lunch. After that, we visited the old town. | Someone called me while I was at the gym. | When I got home, I made some soup.
explanation shown to learner: *before* + subject + verb (*Before I go to work*) or *before* + -ing (*Before going to work*), not *before* + the bare verb.
explanation in Latvian: *before* + teik. priekšmets + darbības vārds (*Before I go to work*) vai *before + -ing* (*Before going to work*), nevis *before go*.

topic: Future: will, going to, present continuous
task: Complete with *will* or *going to*: 'Did you reply to Mark's email?' 'Oh no, I forgot! I ___ to him now.' (write)
explanation shown to learner: The speaker decides now, at the moment of speaking (*Oh no, I forgot!*), so *will* + base verb: *I'll write to him now.* *going to* is for something decided before.
explanation in Latvian: Runātājs pieņem lēmumu tagad, runāšanas brīdī (*I forgot*!), tāpēc *will* + pamatforma: *I'll write to him now.* *going to* lieto, ja lēmums pieņemts jau iepriekš.

topic: Future: will, going to, present continuous
task: Complete with *will* or *going to*: 'Why are you saving so much money?' 'I ___ a flat next year.' (buy)
correct answer: 'm going to buy | am going to buy
explanation shown to learner: The decision was made before (that is why the speaker is saving), so *going to*: *I'm going to buy a flat next year.* *will* is for a decision made at the moment of speaking.
explanation in Latvian: Lēmums pieņemts jau iepriekš (tāpēc runātājs krāj), tāpēc *going to*: *I'm going to buy a flat next year.* *will* lieto lēmumam, ko pieņem runāšanas brīdī.

task: Complete with *a*, *an* or *the*: We always sit at ___ same table in this café.
explanation shown to learner: *same* always has *the* before it: *the same table, the same day*.
explanation in Latvian: Pirms *same* vienmēr lieto *the*: *the same table, the same day*.

task: Correct the mistake: Maria is best driver in our family.
correct answer: Maria is the best driver in our family. | Maria's the best driver in our family.
explanation shown to learner: Before a superlative (*best, biggest, most expensive*) we use *the*: *the best driver*.
explanation in Latvian: Pirms vispārākās pakāpes formas (*best, biggest, most expensive*) lieto *the*: *the best driver*.

topic: Prepositions after words (listen to, good at)
task: Say it another way with *discuss*: We talked about the new timetable at the meeting.
correct answer: We discussed the new timetable at the meeting. | We discussed the new timetable in the meeting. | At the meeting we discussed the new timetable. | At the meeting, we discussed the new timetable.
explanation shown to learner: *talk about* has a preposition, but *discuss* takes its object directly: *We discussed the new timetable*, not *discussed about*.
explanation in Latvian: *talk about* ir ar prievārdu, bet aiz *discuss* papildinātājs seko uzreiz: *We discussed the new timetable*, nevis *discussed about*.
